Behaverse Data Model (BDM) is a dataset structure designed to capture everything a cognitive science study produces: behavioral responses across a wide range of activities (cognitive tests, questionnaires, games), the physiological signals recorded alongside them (EEG, eye tracking, and other continuous measures), and the instructions, task parameters, and metadata needed to interpret any of it. It defines a folder structure, a set of tidy tables, and the conventions that keep them consistent from one study to the next.

<br />

![A typical [workflow](studyflows.qmd) in an experimental study. BDM defines the structure of the experimental design (studyflow), raw observations (events), behavioral data (trials), and downstream analyses (derived models)](../assets/bpmn/behavioral_experiments.png){width="80%" .lightbox}

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-md-6 .g-col-12}

### Conventions

***The rules every BDM dataset follows, whatever it contains:***

[**Naming things**](conventions/naming.qmd)
: How variables, columns, files, values—and the people and tasks they describe—are named, and why.

[**Indexing things**](conventions/indexing.qmd)
: The index variables (agent, session, activity, block, trial, …), what each one means, and how they nest.

[**Units**](conventions/units.qmd)
: How quantities, times, and dates are expressed.

[**Tables**](conventions/tables.qmd)
: The tidy structure every data table follows, and how its rows and columns are ordered.

### Dataset layout

***What a BDM dataset physically is:***

[**Folder structure**](conventions/folder-structure.qmd)
: A BDM dataset is a folder that contains data files and all relevant information needed to make sense of that data.

[**Dataset cards**](dataset-cards.qmd)
: Contain metadata and information about a dataset. Dataset cards also include a codebook to describe the semantics, structure, and format of the data variables.

### Study artifacts

***Descriptions of how the data came to be:***

[**Studyflows**](studyflows.qmd)
: Describe the study protocol and the sequence of activities that agents are exposed to.

[**Instructions**](instructions.qmd)
: Provide additional guidance and help about tasks presented to agents in a study.

[**Questionnaires**](questionnaires.qmd)
: Describe the questions presented to agents and the responses they provide.

:::

::: {.g-col-md-6 .g-col-12}

### Data levels

***The data itself, from raw observations to interpretations:***

[<i class="bi bi-database"></i> **Events**](event/index.qmd)
: Raw data collected during the experiment, stored as NDJSON event streams. This level is the most detailed and is typically sufficient to reproduce the original experiment.

[<i class="bi bi-database"></i> **Trials**](trial/index.qmd)
: BDM considers trials as the core components of cognitive experiments. These are task-specific aggregates, derived from raw events, and typically designed to capture the main features of the scientific experiment.

[<i class="bi bi-database"></i> **Models**](models/index.qmd)
: Summary statistics, scores, or computational models that are derived from trials or events. They address research questions or are used for downstream analyses.

[<i class="bi bi-database"></i> **Timeseries**](timeseries/index.qmd)
: Continuous signals (EEG, eye tracking, physiology): a payload file plus a sidecar metadata file, referenced from the event stream.

### Extensions

[**Extensions**](extensions/index.qmd)
: Planned extensions of BDM beyond cognitive tests and questionnaires—custom tests, video games, task EEG, resting state, compression.
